title: fix: Add support for `~test Array~string~` back in Class
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Add back support for `~test Array~string~`

Context: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/4534#discussion_r1314143825

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

We cannot remove that support as it would be a breaking change. 

Also, if `~test Int` is supported, `~test Array~string~` should be too.

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
author: sidharthv96

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
Can `string.split().length` ever be `0`? My feeling is that it can never be less than `1`, so the following should be safe.

```suggestion
  return string.split(substring).length - 1;
```

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: It can, when the input string is empty. I added the max call while writing the unit test when the "" case was added.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
> It can, when the input string is empty. I added the max call while writing the unit test when the "" case was added.

:facepalm: That's my bad for reviewing your PR too quickly! You're right. `"".split("").length` returns `0`.

There's even a big warning about it on [`String.prototype.split()` MDN page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String/split):
![image](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/assets/19716675/36042193-3aa6-41bf-827a-17f81ee33ef3)

Great call on testing this edge case :smile:

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
If we're `export`-ing this function from the file, it would be helpful to have a TSDoc comment, even if it's super basic and a bit repetitive for such a simple function:

```suggestion
/**
 * Count the number of times the given substring appears in the string.
 *
 * @param string - The input string.
 * @param substring - The string to search for.
 * @returns The number of times the substring appears in the string.
 */
export const countOccurrence = (string: string, substring: string): number => {
```

At some point in the future, we could add an ESLint rule like `"jsdoc/require-jsdoc": ["warn", {"publicOnly":true`}]` to warn us about exported functions that aren't documented.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: I prefer functions that are self explanatory. Comments are useful for explaining complex steps and functions, but seems like an unnecessary addition for simple functions.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
> Comments are useful for explaining complex steps and functions, but seems like an unnecessary addition for simple functions.

I agree! But, I do think if we're exporting a function out of a file, the bar for documenting it is a lot lower, since you can't easily see the source-code of the function (especially if you're minifying code).

I think the name/params for this function are self-explanatory enough that we don't need a TSDoc comment, and it'll only be necessary if we ever add an ESLint rule like `"jsdoc/require-jsdoc": ["warn", {"publicOnly":true}]`.
